candidates.title: Prefer code-pretrained models for discourse state tracking
candidates.rule: For tasks requiring tracking entity/object state across a sequence of natural-language operations, choose models whose pretraining includes substantial code (e.g. GPT-3.5 series) rather than text-only or instruction-tuned text models; instruction tuning or RLHF alone did not produce the ability in this study.
candidates.passage: GPT-3.5 models that have been trained on code systematically outperformed GPT-3 models, including code-davinci-002 that was not trained on human feedback.
candidates.location: Section 4.5, 'Training on Code Encourages Entity Tracking Behavior' / Figure 5
candidates.finding: Across davinci, davinci-instruct-beta, text-davinci-001 (text-only) versus code-davinci-002, text-davinci-002, text-davinci-003 (code+text), only the code-pretrained group beat a strong random baseline on changed-state items; Flan-T5 base/XL mostly echoed the initial state. GPT-4 was better still but its training is undisclosed.
workloads: synthetic boxes entity-tracking task (base, AltForms, AmbiRef, MoveContents splits)
candidates.conditions: 2-shot in-context prompting, greedy decoding, January 2023 OpenAI API snapshots; English only; descriptions fit in the context window.
candidates.limitations: Observational comparison of closed models differing in size and training details, so code pretraining is confounded; accuracy still degrades toward the random baseline after several operations, so these models are not reliable for high-accuracy state tracking.
candidates.validation_test: Run matched open models with and without code-heavy pretraining (e.g. code vs text variants at equal size) on a changed-state-only entity-tracking split and compare accuracy as a function of operation count.

candidates.title: Tune output granularity per model when prompting for multi-entity state
candidates.rule: When prompting for the state of many entities at once, pick the output granularity per model: query all entities in one completion for GPT-style models, but query one entity per prompt for Flan-T5, which otherwise emits only the first entity.
candidates.passage: Flan-T5 frequently only output the state of the first box even when the in-context demonstrations contained final descriptions of all box states.
candidates.finding: The authors adjusted Flan-T5 prompts to one box per query because of truncated outputs, and separately verified that GPT accuracy was lower under one-box-at-a-time prompting than all-boxes-at-once, so the format choice is model-dependent.
workloads: synthetic boxes entity-tracking cloze task with 7 boxes
candidates.conditions: 2-shot demonstrations; Flan-T5 with beam size 3, max 256 tokens; GPT with greedy decoding, max 150 tokens.
candidates.limitations: Reported as a prompting adjustment rather than a systematic ablation; the GPT comparison is a single check with no stated effect size, and results are specific to these 2023 models and this synthetic format.
candidates.validation_test: For your model, run the same multi-entity state query in both formats (all entities per completion vs one per completion) on a held-out set and compare exact-match accuracy and output truncation rates.

reason: The paper tests entity tracking across GPT-3/GPT-3.5/GPT-4/Flan-T5 and finetuned T5, with a reanalysis of an existing benchmark showing trivial-case inflation, and an incidental prompt-format comparison. These support three scoped rules on evaluation design, model selection, and prompt output format.
